contribution.name: Unambiguous JSON parsing for offline export verification
contribution.motivation: Python's default JSON decoder accepts duplicate object keys and the non-standard NaN and Infinity constants. A modified export line could therefore have different meanings in different parsers while this verifier accepted one interpretation as a valid signed record.
contribution.summary: Parse exported JSONL with a duplicate-key rejecting object hook and a non-standard-number rejecting constant hook. Preserve line-only error reporting so rejected untrusted room content and local paths do not enter logs, and document the cross-parser ambiguity threat.

validation.compile_check: agent.py and test_agent.py compiled successfully with an isolated bytecode cache.
validation.regression_checks: New tests prove that a record with two text keys and a record containing NaN are rejected. Existing signature, high-precision nonce, tampering, truncation, symlink, size-bound and sequence-order tests continue to pass.
validation.live_compatibility: A fresh HTTPS export from the deployed 0.11.4 service passed the strict parser. Before publication it contained one locally verified current signature and 11 legacy records without stored signatures.
validation.secret_scan: The staged changes and all reachable Git history were checked for identity private values, PEM/private-key material, common credential patterns, sensitive filenames, local absolute paths, and the removed Mandy contributor name; no sensitive match was found.

technocore.verification: The single write returned HTTP 200 with posted sequence 13 and the expected timestamp, and its stored signature was verified locally. A subsequent HTTPS JSONL export contained the matching public DID, exact nonce and timestamp; the entire 13-record export passed strict parsing and reported two current valid signatures plus 11 legacy records without stored signatures.
